accuracy.evidence: Checked against the PSHE Association Programme of Study KS4 (relationships: respectful communication, managing conflict, online behaviour) and DfE RSHE statutory guidance (respectful relationships; online relationships). Steelmanning attributed to Rapoport's rules as popularised by Daniel Dennett (Intuition Pumps, 2013). Evidence examples checked: Rogers et al. 2023, PLOS Medicine, used National Child Measurement Programme data and found lower obesity in Year 6 girls after the soft drinks levy; the National Literacy Trust annual survey reports reading enjoyment among young people at its lowest level in about two decades; the 2022 UK four-day week pilot (61 companies) reported that 56 continued afterwards. The thread meter is labelled as a teaching model, not a measured scale.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets real beliefs teens hold about disagreement: respect means never disagreeing or a talk must have a winner (challenge tags win/cut, mastery m6), a straw man counts as rebuttal (step 2 options, tag straw), one vivid story or 'everyone knows' is evidence (step 3, tags story/crowd/trust), volume is strength (capitals, tags caps/pile), fast hard replies end online rows (step 4 prediction), and common ground means giving in (tags giveup/trick).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagdisag is built around disagreement moves only: sorting replies by target (idea vs person), choosing the steelman over straw man and weak summaries, ranking support by checkability, a thread temperature gauge driven by six online moves, and picking shared ground from two opposed sides. It differs from flagagree (friend fall-outs for young children), flagrepair (observation-feeling-need repair) and flaglead (leadership styles and coercion). Gate: under 30% shingle overlap with every flagship lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner meets each idea in the lab first: the person-attack replies visibly say nothing about homework; picking a straw man is rejected with the reason; the evidence picks reject the story and capitals; the gauge shows capitals, pile-ons and memes raising heat and questions, agreement and a pause lowering it below 30; the common-ground step shows both sides share three goals. The text then names steelman, straw man and common ground.

predictions.evidence: Two predictions with tempting wrong options the lab then tests: 'summing up their view makes your side look weak' (the 'felt understood' count rises with each steelman), and 'a fast, hard reply shows you will not back down' (on the gauge, capitals and pile-ons push the thread hotter, not calmer).

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six challenge questions with two wrong options each and a named slip for each: 'Honest is fine; insulting is not', 'Knocking down a weak version is a straw man', 'One story is not a pattern', 'Capitals read as shouting', 'A pile-on turns a debate into a crowd against one person', 'Shared ground does not mean giving in', 'Not every talk has a winner'.

readability.evidence: validate_lessons.py passes; kid paragraphs about grade 3.9, adult about 5.7. Canvas cards hold one reply or summary each, and terms (steelman, straw man) are defined in the kid text where first used.

no_filler.evidence: No filler pattern matches. Each step practises one move and every feedback line gives the reason the move helps or hurts; no generic encouragement lines.

mobile.evidence: Checked on 360 px screenshots before and after Show me for every step: the three summary and evidence cards wrap to two or three lines within the canvas, the six common-ground chips sit in a 2 × 3 grid, and the gauge label and calm marker stay visible. Buttons below the canvas repeat every choice in full text.

accessibility.evidence: All moves have buttons with full-text aria-labels ('Summary 2: Phones split attention…', 'Reply in CAPITALS', 'Take a break, reply later'). The canvas aria-label reads the state, e.g. 'Thread temperature 54. Calm is below 30. Moves used 1.' Challenge feedback is aria-live. walk.cjs reports axe (WCAG 2.1 AA) clean in both themes on desktop and iPhone 13 with no console errors.

DfE (2019, updated) Relationships Education, RSE and Health Education statutory guidance

Rogers, N. et al. (2023) PLOS Medicine, soft drinks industry levy and obesity in English primary school children
